blocks.text: The judicial chronicle and the administrative texts have a very precise Arabic: each word has a technical value, and an approximate translation ('condemned' by 'defendant', 'final judgment' by 'first-degree judgment') changes the meaning of the news. In this unit you learn the vocabulary of courts and of the stages of a trial as the press tells you, the language of regulatory texts (articles of law, "is forbidden" , "is allowed," "except"), the vocabulary of administrative documents and practices and the rules of prudence to report a judicial case (presumption of innocence, attribution). The cases of the texts are invented and concern only civil and administrative matters or public events told by the newspapers. Four weeks, in parallel with EGY-13.

rows: B2 · Module B2.1 News and institutions of the European Communities
B2-01 → B2-04; INT-02 (powers, official acts); B1-05 (passive); A2-08 (documents)
20–22 hours · four weeks (weeks 172–175), plus the EGY track in separate blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, root dictionary, voice synthesis scripts, tutor sessions
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. understand a judicial news: courts, parties, stages of the trial, types of judgment, appeals;
2. a precise distinction between accused and convicted, first and final judgment, prosecution and evidence, and
to report them in compliance with the presumption of innocence;
3. read an article in law or regulation: numbering, obligations, prohibitions, exceptions, entry into force;
4. understanding the vocabulary of documents and administrative practices (release, renewal, legalization, appeal);
5. read a judicial or administrative service of 350 words at least 80 words per minute.
